```
357: * @param {{delimiter?: string, header?: boolean, skipEmptyLines?: boolean, trim?: boolean, comment?: string}} [options]
378: * @param {{delimiter?: string, header?: boolean, skipEmptyLines?: boolean, trim?: boolean, comment?: string}} [options]
// 'id,name\n1,"Lin, Bo"\n'
```

## API

### `parse(text, options)`

Returns an array of records. Each record is an array of strings, or an object keyed by the first record's fields when `header` is `true`.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `delimiter` | `','` | Field separator: one UTF-16 code unit other than `"`, CR or LF. |
| `header` | `false` | Use the first record as column names and return objects. |
| `skipEmptyLines` | `false` | Drop lines that contain no characters at all. |

Malformed input throws a `CsvError` with 1-based `line` and `column` properties. Columns count UTF-16 code units. The parser throws the first error it reaches reading left to right:

- an unclosed quoted field, reported at its opening quote;
- a character other than a delimiter or line break after a closing quote, reported at that character;
- a duplicate header name, reported where the second occurrence's field starts;
- in header mode, a record with a different number of fields from the header, reported at column 1 of the line where the record starts. This is checked when the record ends.

Invalid arguments throw `TypeError`: `text` that is not a string, a bad `delimiter`, or `header`/`skipEmptyLines` values that are not booleans. Unknown options are ignored, so one options object can be passed to both `parse` and `stringify`.

### `createParser(options)`

| `header` | none | Array of column names. It is written as the first row, and object records are written in its order, with a missing own property written as an empty field. |

A field is quoted when it contains the delimiter, `"`, CR or LF, or when it begins or ends with a space. A record with a single empty field is written as `""`, so it doesn't turn into an empty line.

For any rows that are non-empty arrays of strings, `parse(stringify(rows, opts), opts)` returns the same rows, whether or not `skipEmptyLines` is set.

## Behavior worth knowing

- A leading byte order mark (U+FEFF) is dropped and does not count as a column. A U+FEFF anywhere else is data.
- Line numbers count every line break, including those inside quoted fields. CRLF counts as one.
- One line break at the end of the input does not start a new record. Every other empty line is the record `['']` unless `skipEmptyLines` is set. The input `'\n'` is therefore `[['']]`.
- Fields are never trimmed. A `"` that is not the first character of a field is an ordinary character.
- `stringify` quotes the first field of its output if the output would otherwise begin with U+FEFF, because `parse` would drop that character as a byte order mark.
- `stringify([], { header })` writes the header row alone. Without `header`, no rows gives `''`.
- Header names become own properties via `Object.fromEntries`, so a column called `__proto__` is kept as data.

content.text:
`parse` and `createParser` now take `trim` and `comment`, both off by default. All 206 tests pass, including the existing ones, and I haven't committed anything.

The streaming tests cover every one- and two-cut split and one-character-per-write splits over a corpus that now includes trim and comment inputs. They run with seven new option sets, so `createParser` matches `parse` for both options, errors included. I also added tests to `test/parse.test.js` and `test/stream.test.js`, and updated `README.md`.

**`trim`**
- Leading and trailing spaces and tabs are removed from unquoted fields.
- Spaces and tabs before an opening `"` and after a closing `"` are allowed and dropped. The quoted content is kept exactly.
- Any other character after a closing quote is still the usual `CsvError`.
- Duplicate-header checks use the trimmed value.
- Trailing whitespace is trimmed with a manual scan rather than a regex, because a regex would be quadratic on a long run of spaces. A test covers this.

**`comment`**
- A line starting with the comment character is skipped with its line break, even at the end of input with no line break. It never becomes a record, and `skipEmptyLines` doesn't treat it as an empty line.
- The comment character is ordinary anywhere else, including inside quoted fields.
- Line numbers in errors still count comment lines.
- It throws `TypeError` unless it is a single UTF-16 code unit other than the delimiter, `"`, CR or LF. That includes `null`, non-strings and `''`; `undefined` means off.

**Choices the spec didn't settle**
- A space or tab that is the delimiter is never trimmed. The delimiter wins, so `delimiter: '\t'` with `trim` still works.
- A line of only spaces and tabs under `trim` is the record `['']`. It has characters, so `skipEmptyLines` keeps it.
- The comment check is on the very first character of the line. A leading BOM is dropped first, but spaces are not, so `  #x` is data even with `trim`.
- For a field with leading spaces or tabs under `trim`, error positions point at the first character after them. For example, an unclosed quote is reported at the `"`.

**`stringify` round trip:** `stringify` ignores `trim` and `comment`, so the README's `parse(stringify(rows, opts), opts)` guarantee no longer holds when those options are used. A field starting with the comment character would be read back as a comment, and a tab at the edge of a field would be trimmed. I noted this in the README rather than changing `stringify`.
